events.title: Dorieus on the Cinyps
events.text: The Spartan prince Dorieus, guided by men of Thera, founds a colony at the mouth of the Cinyps river.

events.title: Spartans driven out
events.text: In the colony's third year, the Libyan Macae and the Carthaginians expel Dorieus's settlers.

events.title: Siege of Barca
events.text: A Persian army from Egypt besieges Barca for nine months and deports many of its people to Bactria.

events.title: Punic Lepcis
events.text: Lepcis, a Phoenician harbour since the 600s BC, lies within Carthage's widening sphere.

events.title: Silphium wealth
events.text: Cyrene grows rich exporting silphium, a resinous plant prized as medicine and seasoning, found only in Cyrenaica.

events.title: Pythian victory
events.text: King Arcesilaus IV of Cyrene wins the chariot race at Delphi, celebrated in two odes by Pindar.

events.title: Sabratha
events.text: A seasonal Phoenician trading beach at Sabratha becomes a permanent town.

events.title: The Battiads fall
events.text: The last Battiad king, Arcesilaus IV, is overthrown; Cyrene becomes a republic.

events.title: Dates of Augila
events.text: Herodotus tells how the Nasamones leave their herds by the sea each summer to harvest dates at Augila.

events.title: The Garamantes
events.text: Herodotus describes a powerful people of the Fezzan who farm the oases and drive four-horse chariots.

events.title: Euhesperides besieged
events.text: Peloponnesian ships blown to Libya help the Greeks of Euhesperides beat off a Libyan siege.

events.title: Strife at Cyrene
events.text: Civil war divides Cyrene; exiled Messenians from Naupactus fight and die in the struggle.

events.title: Legend of the race
events.text: Sallust's undated story: runners leave Carthage and Cyrene on the same day, and the border is fixed where they meet.

events.title: The Philaeni
events.text: Accused of starting early, the Carthaginian brothers Philaeni choose to be buried alive to keep the line.

events.title: Altars on record
events.text: A Greek sailing guide, the Periplus of Pseudo-Scylax, names the Altars of Philaenus as a landmark of the Syrtis.

events.title: Envoys to Alexander
events.text: Cyrene sends gifts and a treaty of friendship to Alexander on his way to the oracle of Ammon at Siwa.

events.title: Thibron's war
events.text: The mercenary captain Thibron seizes Cyrene's harbour and makes war on the cities of Cyrenaica.

events.title: Ophellas takes Cyrene
events.text: Sent by Ptolemy, the general Ophellas defeats Thibron and annexes Cyrenaica to Ptolemaic Egypt.

events.title: A royal charter
events.text: Ptolemy gives Cyrene a new constitution, carved in stone, naming himself its general for life.

events.title: Cyrene revolts
events.text: Cyrene rises against Ptolemy; once it is subdued, Ophellas rules the country as his own.

events.title: Ophellas marches
events.text: Lured by Agathocles of Syracuse, Ophellas leads over ten thousand soldiers and as many camp followers west.

events.title: Across the Syrtis
events.text: After more than two months crossing the waterless shore, Ophellas reaches his ally, who has him murdered near Carthage.

events.title: Magas recovers Cyrene
events.text: Ptolemy's stepson Magas wins Cyrenaica back for Egypt after Ophellas's death.

events.title: King Magas
events.text: Magas proclaims himself king of Cyrene and marches against his half-brother, Ptolemy II of Egypt.

events.title: Marmaridae revolt
events.text: Libyan nomads of Marmarica rise behind Magas's army and force him to turn back.

events.title: Demetrius killed
events.text: Magas's daughter Berenice has her husband, Demetrius the Fair, killed and holds Cyrene for Egypt.

events.title: Berenice of Benghazi
events.text: Berenice marries Ptolemy III; Euhesperides is refounded in her name as Berenice, today's Benghazi.

events.title: Ptolemais
events.text: Barca's harbour is rebuilt as Ptolemais, a royal city of the Ptolemies.

events.title: First Punic War ends
events.text: Carthage loses Sicily to Rome but keeps its African coast, including the Emporia.

events.title: Masinissa's first raid
events.text: The Numidian king raids the Emporia; Rome's envoys, Scipio among them, leave the dispute unsettled.

events.title: Mausoleum at Sabratha
events.text: Sabratha raises a tall Punic tower tomb carved with Egyptian and Greek motifs.

events.title: Ptolemy VIII in Cyrene
events.text: Driven from Alexandria by his brother, Ptolemy VIII is made king of Cyrene alone.

events.title: Masinissa seizes the Emporia
events.text: Numidian forces occupy the Syrtic emporia; Rome backs Masinissa, and Carthage loses the towns and pays five hundred talents.

events.title: A will for Rome
events.text: Ptolemy VIII publishes his will at Cyrene: if he dies without heirs, his kingdom goes to Rome.

events.title: Carthage destroyed
events.text: Rome destroys Carthage; the Punic towns of Tripolitania live on under Numidian kings.

events.title: Rule from Alexandria
events.text: Ptolemy VIII becomes king of Egypt and governs Cyrenaica from Alexandria again.

events.title: Lepcis turns to Rome
events.text: During the war on Jugurtha, Lepcis asks Rome for alliance; Metellus sends four cohorts of Ligurians.

events.title: Ptolemy Apion
events.text: By about 100 BC, Ptolemy Apion, a son of Ptolemy VIII, rules Cyrenaica as a separate kingdom.

events.title: Rome inherits Cyrenaica
events.text: Apion dies and wills his kingdom to Rome; the Senate takes the royal lands and leaves the cities free.

events.title: Garamantes beyond Rome
events.text: Far to the south, the Garamantes remain independent masters of the Saharan oasis routes.

chartNote: Share of the area of modern Libya, by the power that held or claimed the settled part of each present-day district (today's boundaries, not ancient ones). It is a simplification: Libyan peoples lived in every district, the vast Saharan districts swing the shares, and dates before 400 BC are approximate. The Altars of the Philaeni are placed at Ras el-Aali; their true site is unknown.
